source.publication: 2025 Schedule M1M Income Additions and Subtractions
source.section: Form M1 lines 1-4, 7-10 (instructions PDF p.13 Standard Deduction Table for Line 4, p.14 Worksheet A, p.39 Tax Rate Schedules, pp.32-38 tax table); Schedule M1M line 12 and Worksheet for line 12 steps 1-30 (M1M PDF p.3, p.4)

worked: Measure over 69,250: the alternative is reduced 20% of the excess; the simplified method still wins. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages 50,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 = 75,500.00. Social Security benefits (Form 1040 line 6a) 30,000.00; line 6b taxable 25,500.00 (federal worksheet: benefits taxable up to 85%; given, not tested). Federal taxable income = 75,500.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction (15,750 plus 0 x 2,000) = 59,750.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form M1, single: line 1 federal AGI 75,500.00. Schedule M1M line 1 other-state municipal interest 0.00; line 10 additions 0.00; Form M1 line 2 0.00; line 3 = 75,500.00. Schedule M1M line 12: AGI 75,500.00 is not over 84,490.00, so worksheet steps 3-5 give 0 and the simplified amount is all of line 6b, 25,500.00. Alternative method, projection: measure = federal AGI + tax-exempt interest = 75,500.00 + 0.00 = 75,500.00; cap first: lesser of 25,500.00 and 4,560.00 = 4,560.00; less 20% x (excess over 69,250.00, 6,250.00) = 1,250.00; alternative = 3,310.00. Worksheet steps 9-24 as printed: steps 9-11 75,500.00 - 25,500.00 = 50,000.00; steps 12-13 50% x 30,000.00 = 15,000.00; step 14 0.00; step 15 65,000.00; steps 16-18 0.00; step 19 65,000.00; step 20 69,250.00; step 21 0.00; step 22 0.00; step 23 4,560.00; step 24 4,560.00; step 25-27 25,500.00; step 28 4,560.00; step 30 greater of 4,560.00 and 25,500.00 = 25,500.00. Line 12 = the better of the two, 25,500.00. The projection's alternative entry loses, so only the simplified amount is applied. Schedule M1M line 16: no one is 65 or older (born before January 2, 1961), so no Schedule M1R subtraction. Schedule M1M line 40 = Form M1 line 7 subtractions = 25,500.00 + 0.00 + 0.00 + 0.00 = 25,500.00 (lines 12, 16, 17, 25). State income before deduction = 75,500.00 - 25,500.00 = 50,000.00. Standard Deduction Table for Line 4 (PDF p.13): base 14,950.00; AGI is not over 238,950.00, so no Worksheet A. Line 4 = 14,950.00. Form M1 line 8 total = 14,950.00 + 25,500.00 = 40,450.00; line 9 Minnesota taxable income = 75,500.00 - 40,450.00 = 35,050.00. Line 10 tax from the rate schedule (PDF p.39): 5.35% x (32,570.00 - 0.00) = 1,742.495 + 6.80% x (35,050.00 - 32,570.00) = 168.64 = 1,911.135. The tax table (PDF pp.32-38) gives 1,911; expected keeps the schedule formula. Line 16 credits 0.00; state income tax 1,911.14.
accepted_approximations: The alternative Social Security method tests federal AGI plus tax-exempt interest, the nearest available measure. Worksheet step 19 uses total income less taxable benefits plus 50% of all benefits, which no projection measure holds. The cap is applied before the reduction; the worksheet takes the lesser of the reduced cap and taxable benefits.
Tax comes from the rate schedules at every income; below 86,800 of taxable income the booklet requires its 100-wide tax table.
